- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) or trending negative, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates future values; cap forecast at 1.2x recent high or use moving average of last 5 days for smoothing.
- Model consistently underestimates true values in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 2–3% buffer to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.1 in 3–5 days), model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 1–2 day lagged sentiment adjustment to forecast slope.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model exhibits mean reversion bias — over-predicts if recent price is above 30-day moving average; use 30-day MA as floor for forecast unless sentiment strongly supports upside.
